get.description: Check that the API can reach its database.

post.description:
Resume the visitor's session, or start a guest account and its session.

A valid session gets a later expiry and a fresh cookie. With no cookie, or
a cookie for an expired, unknown or adopted session, the visitor gets a
new guest account. The API deletes the session that cookie named. A
client network can start 30 guest accounts a minute. Past that, the API
answers 429.

The account's player is the one it plays as. Every account has one. A
new player gets a default display name, such as `excited egret 387`. A
verified account has its email. `permissions` lists what the account's
roles let it do, such as `admin.view`.

429.description: The client's network started too many guest accounts. Retry-After gives the seconds until it can start more.

Retry-After.description: The seconds until the network can start more

get.description:
Send the visitor to the identity provider's sign-in page.

A request with no valid session gets no guest account. It gets a login
cookie instead, which the callback checks. After sign-in, the callback
sends the visitor to `return_to`. It must be a path
on this site, or the callback uses `/`.

Such a login counts toward the guest account limit. Past it, the visitor
goes to `/signed-out` with `sign_in_error=rate_limited` and
`retry_after`, the seconds until the network can sign in again.

503.description: The API has no identity provider configured

get.description:
Finish a sign-in, then send the visitor back to its `return_to`.

A successful sign-in adds `signed_in=1` to that path's query. A failed
sign-in adds `sign_in_error` instead: `cancelled`, `email_not_verified`,
`expired` or `failed`. A callback from another browser gets `failed`, and
keeps the login cookie, which may belong to a newer sign-in. A callback
whose `state` matches no login attempt, such as a replay, goes to `/`
with `sign_in_error=used`.

503.description: The API has no identity provider configured

post.description:
Start a sign-in from the native app.

The app opens `authorize_url` in a browser of its own. That browser has
none of the app's cookies, so the provider sends it to `app-callback`,
which hands the query back to the app, and the app finishes the sign-in
with `app-finish`. Like `login`, a request with no valid session gets no
guest account, but a login cookie that `app-finish` checks.
`authorize_url` can be relative to the API's origin.

429.description: The client's network started too many guest accounts. Retry-After gives the seconds until it can start more.

Retry-After.description: The seconds until the network can start more

503.description: The API has no identity provider configured

get.description:
Send the provider's redirect on to the native app.

It answers 302 to `fortymm://sign-in` with this request's query, which
the app passes to `app-finish`. Another app that claims the scheme gets
nothing it can use, because finishing needs the app's session or login
cookie.

post.description:
Finish a sign-in that `app-login` started, with the query that
`app-callback` handed to the app.

`outcome` is `signed_in`, or why the sign-in failed: `cancelled`,
`email_not_verified`, `expired` or `failed`. A sign-in sets a new session
cookie. A `state` that matches no login attempt, such as a replay, is
`expired`. A failed sign-in changes no account. A request from another
browser is `failed`, and keeps the login cookie.

503.description: The API has no identity provider configured

post.description:
End the visitor's session and expire its cookie.

`logout_url` is the identity provider's logout page. The client follows
it, so the provider's own session ends too. The provider then sends the
browser to `/signed-out`, which starts no session. `/` would start a new
guest account, and it wouldn't look like a sign-out.

503.description: The API has no identity provider configured

get.description:
List the players the account manages, its own player first. A merged
player isn't listed.

`open_question` is true for a player that a sign-in brought to the
account, until the account answers "Is this you?" for it.
`match_count` counts the player's matches, and `recent_matches` holds
its latest ones, newest first.

401.description: The request has no valid session

post.description:
Answer "Is this you?" for one player. `data` lists the account's
players after the answer, and `meta.outcome` says what the answer did.

`yes` makes it the account's own player, with outcome `self`. If the
account already has one, the two players merge, with outcome `merged`.
`no` keeps it as a player the account manages, with outcome `managed`.
`not_mine` takes it off the account, with outcome `removed`. The player
stays, with no manager. `same_as` merges it with the `managed` player
that `player_id` names, with outcome `merged`. That player's question
must be closed, because the merge would close it with no answer.

In a merge, the player created first survives, and the other leaves the
list. `meta.survivor` and `meta.merged` name them. Every answer closes
the question. A second answer changes nothing, with outcome
`already_answered`, but a second `not_mine` answers 409.

401.description: The request has no valid session

404.description: The account doesn't manage the player, or `player_id` isn't a `managed` player of the account with a closed question

409.description: The answer is `not_mine` and the question was already answered

422.description: The body is invalid, or `player_id` is missing with `same_as` or set with another answer. If `player_id` is the answered player, the body is in the `errors` shape instead

get.description:
List every permission by key, with how many roles grant it. Needs
`admin.view`.

A `built_in` permission is one the code checks, such as `admin.view`.

401.description: The request has no valid session

403.description: The account's roles don't grant the permission the route needs

post.description:
Add a permission that roles can grant. Needs `roles.manage`.

Code that checks its key can come later. The key never changes.

401.description: The request has no valid session

403.description: The account's roles don't grant the permission the route needs

401.description: The request has no valid session

403.description: The account's roles don't grant the permission the route needs

delete.description:
Delete a permission. Every role that granted it loses it. Needs
`roles.manage`. A built-in permission can't be deleted.

401.description: The request has no valid session

403.description: The account's roles don't grant the permission the route needs

409.description: The permission is built in, because the code checks it

get.description:
List every role by name, with its permissions and how many accounts
hold it. Needs `admin.view`.

401.description: The request has no valid session

403.description: The account's roles don't grant the permission the route needs

post.description:
Create a role with these permissions. Needs `roles.manage`.

The name is trimmed, and two roles can't share one, whatever its case.
A permission key that names no permission answers 422.

401.description: The request has no valid session

403.description: The account's roles don't grant the permission the route needs

409.description: Another role has this name, whatever its case

422.description: The body is invalid. If a permission key names no permission, the body is in the `errors` shape instead

put.description:
Set the role's name, description and exact set of permissions. Needs
`roles.manage`.

The API answers 409 if another role has the name, or if the change
would leave no account with `account_roles.manage`.

401.description: The request has no valid session

403.description: The account's roles don't grant the permission the route needs

422.description: The body is invalid. If a permission key names no permission, the body is in the `errors` shape instead

409.description: Another role has this name, or the change would leave no account with `account_roles.manage`

delete.description:
Delete the role. Every account that held it loses it. Needs
`roles.manage`.

The API answers 409 if no account would keep `account_roles.manage`.

401.description: The request has no valid session

403.description: The account's roles don't grant the permission the route needs

409.description: The change would leave no account with `account_roles.manage`, so nobody could grant a role again

get.description:
List the verified accounts by email, with the roles each holds. Needs
`admin.view`.

`email` keeps the accounts whose email contains it, whatever its case.
The list holds at most 50. `meta.has_more` says that more match.

401.description: The request has no valid session

403.description: The account's roles don't grant the permission the route needs

get.description:
The verified account, with every role and whether it holds each, for
its admin page. Needs `admin.view`.

401.description: The request has no valid session

403.description: The account's roles don't grant the permission the route needs

404.description: No verified account has this id

put.description:
Give the account exactly these roles. Needs `account_roles.manage`.

Only a verified account holds roles. The API answers 409 if no account
would keep `account_roles.manage`, such as when the last administrator
revokes their own role.

401.description: The request has no valid session

403.description: The account's roles don't grant the permission the route needs

404.description: No verified account has this id, or a role doesn't exist

409.description: The change would leave no account with `account_roles.manage`, so nobody could grant a role again
